Committee: State Government
Sponsor: Robbins
Analyst: Vee Mosely
Date: 03/14/2022
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 463 as introduced proposes a Constitutional Amendment which, if ratified, would increase the administrative obligations of the Department of Conservation and Natural Resources to market carbon credits for at least 50% of all Forever Wild Land Trust property located in Coosa County. This bill would also increase receipts to the Coosa County general fund by an undetermined amount dependent on the amount of income from carbon credits generated from the management of Forever Wild Forest resources located in Coosa County, as provided by this bill.
This bill would also increase the proclamation expenses of the Governor, paid from the State General Fund, by either an estimated $1,500 or $100,000 for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2023, dependent upon if voted on locally or statewide, respectively.
Chris Pringle, Chair
State Government

Committee: Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry
Sponsor: Robbins
Analyst: Vee Mosely
Date: 03/30/2022
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 463 as passed the House of Representatives proposes a Constitutional Amendment which, if ratified, would increase the administrative obligations of the Department of Conservation and Natural Resources to market carbon credits for at least 50% of all Forever Wild Land Trust property located in Coosa County. This bill would also increase receipts to the Coosa County general fund by an undetermined amount dependent on the amount of income from carbon credits generated from the management of Forever Wild Forest resources located in Coosa County, as provided by this bill.
This bill would also increase the proclamation expenses of the Governor, paid from the State General Fund, by either an estimated $1,500 or $100,000 for the fiscal year ending September 30, 2023, dependent upon if voted on locally or statewide, respectively.
As amended and reported by the Committee on Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry, changes the minimum amount of carbon credits that may be marketed by the Department from at least 50% of all Forever Wild Land Trust Property to at least 10% of all Forever Wild Land Trust Property.
Larry Stutts, Chairperson
Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry
